A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Tree-of-Debate research. Their main text, figures, tables, mathematical notation, and appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original domain-expert evaluations on 100 paper pairs, including comparisons with baselines, ablations, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds expert-agreement measurements, domain breakdowns, retrieval and model comparisons, depth experiments, and error analyses.

M1.justification: The personas, iterative retrieval, preemption, debate rounds, expansion rules, and final synthesis remain unchanged. The prompts in v1 Appendix G match v2 Appendix M after reference renumbering. Testing alternative backbones does not revise the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain 100 paper pairs across NLP, data mining, electrical engineering, and aerospace engineering, with the same task/method and citation-status categories. The added analyses examine retained coverage; they do not establish new datasets, domains, or task requirements.

E2.justification: The main comparison retains Single Stage, Two Stage, No Tree, and No SD. v2 additionally evaluates intfloat/e5-large-v2 against the BGE retriever through the retrieved-segment comparison in Table 7, adding a limited comparison of retrieval components.

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols compare 8B, 32B, and 70B backbones, vary debate depth from 1 to 3, inspect the top four retrieved segments, and obtain overlapping expert ratings. The original benchmark, metrics, default retrieval count of five, branching factor of three, and maximum depth of three remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends the diagnostic evidence beyond the retained No Tree/No SD ablations and existing cases. Section 5.2 and Appendices F–I add domain analysis, retrieval and backbone sensitivity studies, depth sensitivity, and concrete factuality, breadth, and contextualization errors. These investigate previously untested component dependencies and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Appendix E adds a targeted inter-expert reliability study: annotation agreement, rating agreement, an ordinal agreement index, and factuality ICC estimates. v1 only reports dispersion across comparison settings. The new study concerns overlapping NLP/data-mining expertise, leaves its evaluation subset size unspecified, and adds no repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2's corresponding scores are unchanged, but Tables 5–9 and Appendix I add substantial domain, agreement, retrieval, model, depth, and error findings. For example, aerospace factuality is newly reported as 88.64 for ToD versus 97.14 for Two Stage. The retrieval-ablation discussion also revises contextualization averages: No SD changes from 91.37 to 91.59 and Two Stage from 75.57 to 75.80. These are additions and numerical revisions, not evidence of improved same-setting performance.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and mathematical description of the debate tree are retained, with no new assumptions, theorems, or proofs. Appendix C merely spells out normalization of the existing rating scale.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: paper personas and structured debate trees produce informative, contextualized scientific comparisons. The added evidence does not redefine the claimed contribution.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation beyond v1's general factuality warning. Sections 5.2–5.4 and Appendices F–I discuss domain and backbone dependence, explain depth effects, and identify confusion between papers as a principal factuality failure. The engineering-domain factuality deficits and concrete error cases provide more specific qualifications of the method's strengths.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5, clarifies expert selection of meaningful paper pairs and existing score normalization, and replaces the anonymous dataset access address with a GitHub dataset directory. These improve documentation; the original hyperparameters, hardware specification, and main code link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the error cases and CoT/ToT examples, including Kumari et al., Renduchintala et al., Sener and Savarese, Wei et al., and Yao et al. Section 2's related-work discussion and the central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main section order are retained. v2 adds focused results subsections and acknowledgements, edits several headings and explanations, and reorganizes appendices, including moving dataset specifications from E to L and prompts from G to M.

P2.justification: v2 adds five analysis tables, reformats the existing debate-path example as Table 12, moves Figure 1 onto the opening page, reorders Table 2's method rows, and color-codes argument strength in Table 3. Existing dataset and summary tables are relocated and reformatted, producing substantial changes to the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides useful reliability checks, targeted sensitivity studies, clearer domain-specific weaknesses, and concrete error explanations. These make the empirical claims easier to assess while preserving the original results. The gains remain limited: sensitivity studies use one paper pair, and the agreement study leaves its subset size unspecified, so the additions provide only narrow validation.
